faq.a: Hafizah is associated with the Arabic form حفيظة, whose core sense is protector, guardian, preserver.

faq.q: What is the origin of Hafizah?
faq.a: Hafizah is associated with Arabic. Hafizah is Arabic حفيظة (Ḥafīẓa) 'guardian, preserver (feminine)'. The source gloss 'guardian of the Quran' mixes the lexical sense with the usage title; both are recorded.
Yes — the underlying form حفيظة is Arabic.
Hafizah can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Hafizah should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. True

faq.q: What does Hafizah mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Hafizah is rendered حفیظہ and carries the sense محافظ، نگہبان.

faq.q: What does Hafizah mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Hafizah is rendered حفیظه and carries the sense نگهبان، نگاه‌دارنده.
A romanized syllable approximation is ha-fi-zah. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Hafizah?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Hafizah, hafizah. Script forms are حفيظة, حفیظه, حفیظہ, हफ़ीज़ा.

faq.q: Is Hafizah a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
